newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy opposition mulls confidence vote on TV bill.
newsitem.headline: Italy opposition mulls confidence vote on TV bill.

text.p: The centre-right Forza Italia party of Italian opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi was considering forcing a confidence vote on a bill it fears could hurt private broadcasters, a senior party member said Tuesday.
"If we're not convinced by the text, we have all the elements to force the government to call a confidence vote," said Paolo Romani, the Forza Italia deputy responsible for the information sector.
Berlusconi's Mediaset company operates three national stations.

The centre-right objects to the possibility that the bill could grant privileges not applicable to private broadcasters to state broadcaster Rai and soon-to-be-privatised telecommunications holding Stet.
The bill also sets up a watchdog body to regulate the future deregulated broadcasting sector.

The centre-right Freedom Alliance bloc said in a statement its would mount a "clear and determined opposition battle in the Chamber." The bill is due to pass to the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on Wednesday.
"We cannot understand why the majority persists in considering Rai above the rules that are valid for everyone else," the Freedom Alliance statement said.
Rai and Mediaset have roughly equal audience share.

The ruling centre-left majority remains confident that the bill will be approved by a July 31 deadline. The centre-left earlier overcame objections from the hard-left Communist Refoundation party concerning an amendment relating to digital broadcasting.
Post and Communications Minister Antonio Maccanico said he did not know whether a confidence vote would be called. "That's a decision that's up to (Prime Minister Romano Prodi)," he said.
A confidence vote cannot be held until 24 hours after it has been called.
